description: A composite of two bright-field TEM micrographs, mounted side by side, showing the dislocation structures produced by deforming Fe–35% Al. The left-hand image is the lower-magnification field: a black scale bar labelled "0.25 µm" sits at its lower right, and a black arrow at lower centre points down-right, marking the imaging vector g = 1 1 0. It shows a dense tangle of curved and straight dislocation lines crossing the foil, with many short, closely spaced near-parallel segments appearing as dipoles, plus long straight near-screw dislocations running in a common direction. The right-hand image is a higher-magnification view of the same microstructure with a "0.1 µm" scale bar and its own arrowed imaging vector; here individual dislocation lines, long straight superdislocations and bowed dipole segments pulled out of moving screws are resolved, and one region is annotated with the lower-case letter "d" whose meaning the caption does not define. Both images were taken with the zone axis near [1 1 0]. No axes, plots or numeric values other than the two scale bars are printed.

observations.observation: Both panels are bright-field TEM micrographs of deformed Fe–35% Al, imaged with the zone axis near [1 1 0].
The left micrograph carries a scale bar labelled 0.25 µm and the right micrograph carries a scale bar labelled 0.1 µm, so the right panel is the higher-magnification view.
Each panel contains a black arrow that the caption identifies as marking the imaging vector 1 1 0.
The right-hand micrograph shows a region annotated with the lower-case letter 'd'; the caption does not define this label.
The caption states that many edge dipole segments are visible, some being dragged out of a glissile screw dislocation at right.
The citing text states that the dislocations present are superdislocations of the B2 lattice, constituted by two partials of Burgers vector (1/2)111 lying close to each other.
The citing text describes Fig. 17 as showing many straight, near-screw superdislocations and edge dipole segments seen as widely spaced dislocations.
The citing text reports that dipole segments are pulled out of moving screw superdislocations where these encounter an obstacle.
Visually, both panels show a dense network of long, nearly straight dislocation lines together with numerous short, closely spaced parallel segments consistent with dipoles.
No axes, numerical data labels or legends are printed in either panel; the only printed values are the two scale-bar lengths (0.25 µm and 0.1 µm).

subfigures.description: Lower-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph of deformed Fe–35% Al with a 0.25 µm scale bar at lower right and a black arrow at lower centre marking the imaging vector 1 1 0. Shows a dense network of curved and straight dislocation lines with numerous short, closely spaced dipole segments and straight near-screw dislocations.

Higher-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph of the same alloy with a 0.1 µm scale bar, its own arrowed imaging vector, and a region annotated with the letter 'd'. Resolves individual dislocations, long straight segments and bowed dipole segments; some segments appear to be dragged out of moving screw dislocations.

unreadable_items: The arrows in both panels are unlabelled; their identity as the 1 1 0 imaging vector comes only from the caption, not from printed text in the image.
The meaning of the letter 'd' annotation in the right-hand micrograph is not stated in the caption and cannot be determined from the pixels.
